title: st reopen realises a dehydrated thread's views but not its attachments, and the canon gate refuses the next commit
body:
`intent st reopen ST0069 --reason "..."` on 2026-09-13 (the thread was Completed and dehydrated, not declared in `.intentfiles`) re-declared it and realised its tree: info.md, acceptance.md and every WP's info.md, but NOT its attachment `design.md`, which the canon (`intent/.canon/st/ST0069.json`) carries. The next commit was refused by `canon_commit_check.sh`: "the index (staged) names bytes it does not contain: ST0069/design.md". `intent organize -v` then listed `intent/st/ST0069/design.md` as the one path to hydrate, and `organize --apply` wrote it; the commit went through with it. So a state verb that realises a thread's tree realises its views and leaves its attachments to `organize`, and the gate sees the gap first. Either the realise path writes attachments with the views, or the verb's output says the tree is partial and names `organize`.

CLOSED 2026-09-14 21:04Z: A state verb whose list edit re-lists a thread (st reopen, and every verb that re-declares on the way back to WIP) now realises the thread's files through Facade::hydration, the one realise path st hydrate uses, so its attachments are written with its views and the next commit's canon gate has them. The status and list edit land first, so a realisation that fails is a warning naming `intent organize --apply` rather than the verb's error (0376's rule). With 0343 in the same commit. Fixed in the commit that closes this issue.
